pages.name: The fastest gear
pages.task: The motor turns the first 12‑tooth pinion. Which gear turns fastest?
pages.why: The 36‑tooth wheel turns at a third of the motor's speed. The second pinion turns with it. The output wheel turns at a third of that again: a ninth of the motor's speed. So the motor pinion turns fastest.
pages.alt: A motor turns a 12-tooth gear clockwise. That drives a 36-tooth gear anticlockwise, and a 12-tooth gear fixed to the same shaft turns with it. That drives a 36-tooth gear clockwise. The counters read: motor pinion 3 turns, 36-tooth wheel 1 turn, second pinion 1 turn, output wheel 0 turns. Picked: the motor pinion.

pages.name: One shaft, one speed
pages.text: After nine turns of the motor pinion, the wheel and the second pinion both show three turns. The output wheel shows one.
pages.alt: A motor turns a 12-tooth gear clockwise. That drives a 36-tooth gear anticlockwise, and a 12-tooth gear fixed to the same shaft turns with it. That drives a 36-tooth gear clockwise. The counters read: motor pinion 9 turns, 36-tooth wheel 3 turns, second pinion 3 turns, output wheel 1 turn.

pages.name: Count the turns
pages.task: The motor pinion turns 18 times. How many turns does the output wheel make?
pages.why: 18 ÷ 3 = 6 turns of the middle shaft. So the second pinion turns 6 times too. Then 6 ÷ 3 = 2 turns of the output wheel.
pages.alt: A motor turns a 12-tooth gear clockwise. That drives a 36-tooth gear anticlockwise, and a 12-tooth gear fixed to the same shaft turns with it. That drives a 36-tooth gear clockwise. The counters read: motor pinion 18 turns, 36-tooth wheel 6 turns, second pinion 6 turns, output wheel 2 turns.

pages.name: Ratios multiply
pages.text: With 12, 36, 12 and 36 teeth, the stages read 3 : 1 and 3 : 1. The overall ratio reads 9 : 1.
pages.alt: A motor turns a 12-tooth gear clockwise. That drives a 36-tooth gear anticlockwise, and a 12-tooth gear fixed to the same shaft turns with it. That drives a 36-tooth gear clockwise.

pages.name: The motor's speed
pages.task: A motor turns at 1450 rev/min. Its 15-tooth pinion drives a 45-tooth wheel. A 12-tooth pinion on that shaft drives a 48-tooth wheel. How fast does the output wheel turn?
pages.why: 45 ÷ 15 = 3 and 48 ÷ 12 = 4. So the overall ratio is 3 × 4 = 12. Then 1450 ÷ 12 = 120.8 rev/min.
pages.alt: A motor turns a 15-tooth gear clockwise. That drives a 45-tooth gear anticlockwise, and a 12-tooth gear fixed to the same shaft turns with it. That drives a 48-tooth gear clockwise.

pages.name: Speed for torque
pages.text: From the motor to the drum, the speed bar falls to a ninth. The torque bar grows nine times. The power bar keeps one length.
pages.alt: A motor turns a 12-tooth gear clockwise. That drives a 36-tooth gear anticlockwise, and a 12-tooth gear fixed to the same shaft turns with it. That drives a 36-tooth gear clockwise. The last shaft carries a winch drum, and its cable holds a load. Speed, torque and power on the motor, middle and drum shafts. From the motor to the drum the speed bar falls 9 times and the torque bar grows 9 times. The power bars are all the same height.

pages.name: Faster and stronger
pages.task: Can a gear train make its output turn faster than the motor and with more torque?
pages.answer: No, it trades one for the other
pages.why: Power is torque × speed. In an ideal train it stays the same. Friction only takes some away. So the output can turn faster only with less torque. It gets more torque only by turning slower.
pages.alt: A motor turns a 12-tooth gear clockwise. That drives a 36-tooth gear anticlockwise, and a 12-tooth gear fixed to the same shaft turns with it. That drives a 36-tooth gear clockwise. The last shaft carries a winch drum, and its cable holds a load. Speed, torque and power on the motor, middle and drum shafts. From the motor to the drum the speed bar falls 9 times and the torque bar grows 9 times. The power bars are all the same height.
options: No, it trades one for the other

pages.name: The winch drum
pages.text: The load pulls on the cable at the drum's rim. So the drum needs a torque of pull × radius. That is 5000 N × 0.2 m = 1000 N m. An ideal 50 : 1 train divides that by 50. So the motor gives just 20 N m.
pages.alt: A motor turns a 12-tooth gear clockwise. That drives a 60-tooth gear anticlockwise, and a 10-tooth gear fixed to the same shaft turns with it. That drives a 100-tooth gear clockwise. The last shaft carries a winch drum of 0.2 m radius, and its cable holds a load pulling with 5 kN.

pages.name: The motor's torque
pages.task: A winch drum of 0.25 m radius takes a 4 kN pull. Its ideal train is 40 : 1. What torque must the motor give?
pages.why: 4000 × 0.25 = 1000 N m at the drum. Then 1000 ÷ 40 = 25 N m at the motor.

pages.name: Split the ratio
pages.text: One pair stops at about 10 : 1. Past that, the wheel grows huge beside its pinion. So a bigger ratio takes a second stage. To get 20 : 1 from two stages, pick stage ratios that multiply to 20, such as 4 × 5. A 12-tooth pinion into a 48-tooth wheel gives 4 : 1. A 12-tooth pinion into a 60-tooth wheel gives 5 : 1.
pages.alt: A motor turns a 12-tooth gear clockwise. That drives a 48-tooth gear anticlockwise, and a 12-tooth gear fixed to the same shaft turns with it. That drives a 60-tooth gear clockwise.

pages.name: Two equal stages
pages.task: You need 36 : 1 from two equal stages. Each pinion has 15 teeth. How many teeth must each wheel have?
pages.why: 6 × 6 = 36, so each stage is 6 : 1. Each wheel has 15 × 6 = 90 teeth.
pages.alt: A motor turns a 15-tooth gear clockwise. That drives a 90-tooth gear anticlockwise, and a 15-tooth gear fixed to the same shaft turns with it. That drives a 90-tooth gear clockwise.

pages.name: Speeding up
pages.task: The crank turns the 48‑tooth wheel. Which gear turns fastest?
pages.why: 48 ÷ 16 = 3. So the 16‑tooth pinion and the 40‑tooth wheel turn 3 times as fast as the crank. Then 40 ÷ 10 = 4. So the 10‑tooth pinion turns 3 × 4 = 12 times as fast. When a train speeds up at every stage, its last gear is the fastest.
pages.alt: A crank turns a 48-tooth gear clockwise. That drives a 16-tooth gear anticlockwise, and a 40-tooth gear fixed to the same shaft turns with it. That drives a 10-tooth gear clockwise. Picked: the 10‑tooth pinion.

pages.name: Three stages
pages.task: A motor turns at 2400 rev/min. Its three stages are 2 : 1, 3 : 1 and 5 : 1. How fast does the output turn?
pages.alt: A motor turns a 12-tooth gear clockwise. That drives a 24-tooth gear, and a 12-tooth gear fixed to the same shaft turns with it. That drives a 36-tooth gear, and a 12-tooth gear fixed to the same shaft turns with it. That drives a 60-tooth gear.

pages.name: Which way
pages.task: The motor turns clockwise. Which way does the output turn?
pages.why: Three stages make three flips. The two gears on each shaft turn the same way, so they add no flip. So the output turns anticlockwise.
pages.alt: A motor turns a 12-tooth gear clockwise. That drives a 24-tooth gear anticlockwise, and a 12-tooth gear fixed to the same shaft turns with it. That drives a 36-tooth gear clockwise, and a 12-tooth gear fixed to the same shaft turns with it. That drives a 60-tooth gear anticlockwise.
